overview: This exercise used morning and evening student accounts to explore identity management and authorization. I tested both allowed behavior and rejection messages so the account and folder policies could be checked in practice.
environment: Staff share with Morning and Evening folders

steps.title: Join the client to the lab domain
steps.description: I joined the Windows client to the domain so it could use centralized directory accounts and policy settings.

steps.title: Organize the directory objects
steps.description: I used Active Directory Users and Computers to create organizational units and keep the lab accounts and groups organized.

steps.title: Create the student accounts
steps.description: I provisioned the morning and evening student accounts and verified the account inventory.

steps.title: Create and populate the security groups
steps.description: I created AMG and PMG and placed the corresponding students in each group so folder permissions could be assigned through group membership.

steps.title: Configure permitted logon hours
steps.description: I set a morning logon window for the designated account, then tested a logon outside that permitted window.

steps.title: Restrict the approved workstation
steps.description: I set the designated account’s Log On To list to PC01 and tested an attempt from the unapproved workstation.

steps.title: Configure and test account expiration
steps.description: I set an account expiration date and checked the expired-account rejection on the client.

steps.title: Disable an account
steps.description: I disabled the selected evening account and retained the directory confirmation of that change.

steps.title: Configure the Staff share
steps.description: I enabled sharing on the parent Staff folder. The captured share layer grants Everyone broad access, with the underlying NTFS entries controlling the subfolders.

steps.title: Separate the Morning folder permissions
steps.description: I disabled inheritance for the department folder and applied explicit morning and evening group entries as required by the exercise.

steps.title: Configure the Evening folder permissions
steps.description: I configured the evening group’s entries on its folder rather than relying on the same inherited policy as the Morning folder.

steps.title: Test allowed and rejected folder access
steps.description: I used the morning account to open its permitted folder and then attempted the Evening folder. The screenshots show the permitted browse and the rejected access.

checks.title: Account lifecycle restrictions
checks.description: The screenshots show time, workstation and expiration restrictions with their client rejection prompts, plus account disabling.

checks.title: Group-based folder separation
checks.description: The permission views and client tests show different outcomes for the Morning and Evening resources.

checks.title: Inheritance changes
checks.description: The report describes disabling inherited permissions before applying the department-specific entries.

lessons: Groups make role-based permission management easier to maintain than many individual grants.
Authentication restrictions and resource permissions control different parts of access.
Network access must satisfy both share and NTFS permissions; inherited and explicit entries need careful review.
The exercise’s Full Control grants are broader than typical student needs. A practical least-privilege design should choose narrower rights such as Read or Modify where appropriate.
scope: These tests demonstrate department separation and account restrictions. They do not prove that the broad share policy, explicit deny entries or Full Control grants are the minimum permissions appropriate for a real organization.
